correctness.rationale: The pseudoinverse formula gives N_G(X)=X^(1/2)P_X X^(1/2) between 0 and X. The function vanishes at zero, so one can take its trace on the compression to the range of A^(1/2)G; compression Jensen gives the lower bound tr(P_A f(A)). For the remaining comparison, restrict to the common support of A and f(A) and choose a fixed full-column-rank basis for the projected sketch range. Along the positive diagonal interpolation D_t, the evolving basis Y satisfies Y'=H_tY. Differentiating P_tY=Y and P_t²=P_t gives the two off-diagonal blocks of P_t′ in (7). Since (P_t)_ii=∑_j |(P_t)_ij|², symmetrizing produces exactly the covariance sum (8). Each product is nonnegative by monotonicity of f and monotonicity of λ/f(λ) from scalar concavity and f(0)=0. Integrating proves the stated orientation. The empty support or projected sketch gives zero on both sides; rank deficiencies otherwise are handled by the same range argument. Both residuals are PSD, making the nuclear equivalence exact. In the two-dimensional witness the trace comparison squares to 153>125 and the determinant of the difference of the two scaled rank-one outer products is −4/(15√(17/5)), excluding Loewner dominance.
residual_risks: The reported 38,400 checks include path-derivative evaluations and are not 38,400 independent draws. Positive spectra, random sketches, selected functions and path points do not test every hypothesis; the proof supplies the all-rank and boundary cases. No claim of a full numerical rerun or formal verification.

value.rationale: When the same fixed sketch is available for both orders, the theorem answers which order gives smaller nuclear error for every realized sketch, rather than which has a better tail estimate in expectation. The ordered reweighting lemma explains the comparison and extends beyond the fractional powers to practically relevant log and ridge functions. The explicit indefinite difference marks a meaningful limit of the guarantee.
residual_risks: No conclusion about independent sketches, other residual norms, separately truncated approximants, or finite-precision performance.
